answer: Falcon sensor audit: each fake identity needs its own physical camera, about $40 plus 1 hour of enrolment per fake. At join, a camera's PRNU noise print is enrolled. Each epoch the beacon flashes a random lotus glyph in saffron-tinted frames; the agent must return a fresh photo of it within 10 s. Graders check the photo's sensor noise against the enrolled print and every other print: a mismatch fails, a collision merges both identities. A farm cannot share one camera (prints collide) or pre-render (glyph unknown until the beacon). Limit: cheap phones still scale linearly.
